value.body: A business analyst studies how a business or process works, finds problems, and translates needs into clear requirements or data-backed recommendations. Employers include IT services and consulting firms, banks, product companies and analytics teams. A typical day involves meetings with users, writing requirement documents, analysing data in Excel or SQL, and working with developers or managers.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA, B.Com, B.A. Economics, B.Sc Statistics or B.Tech; MBA for some roles

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, SQL, Power BI or Tableau, Jira, flowchart tools

items.label: Tech industry workforce
items.note: Direct employees, FY2026 estimate; ~58 lakh in FY2025

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often join as associate or junior analysts in IT services, consulting or analytics firms, sometimes after a support or testing role. Skills in Excel, SQL and a dashboard tool, shown through a few small projects, help in interviews.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Clear communication with business and tech teams

value.title: At a glance
items: The title means different things at different employers, so job descriptions matter.
Next roles: senior analyst, product manager, consultant.
An MBA is common for moving into strategy roles, but not required.

competition.note: BA (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
